sections.h2: Who sends the bill and keeps the maps
sections.html:
One department at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor handles both Tax Collections and Tax Mapping. The tax line, (252) 794-5310, takes bill and payment questions. The mapping line, (252) 794-5311, covers parcels, maps and ownership by street address.

Under Online Services on the county website you will find a tax bill payment page and a real property search. Because the register of deeds indexes only by name, anyone who has just an address should call the mapping line first.

  • Bills and payments: (252) 794-5310
  • Parcels, maps and address lookups: (252) 794-5311
  • Recording and deed indexes: our Bertie County register of deeds page

Farm and timber land dominate Bertie. Windsor is the seat, and eight towns are incorporated: Askewville, Aulander, Colerain, Kelford, Lewiston-Woodville, Powellsville, Roxobel and Windsor. Population is 17,086, drifting lower each year. The county has 9,116 housing units, with 72.7 percent of homes lived in by their owners and a typical value of $98,500. With homes that affordable, back taxes can eat a big share of a sale price, so tidy the tax record before you list.

Land records here carry a state-required flag on any tract lying within half a mile of a farm in a voluntary agricultural district, so a buyer searching title will learn about the farm next door.

Current values in Bertie come from January 1, 2020. The state's schedule has the next reappraisal in 2028, which stays within the eight-year ceiling.

In the years between reappraisals, a value changes mainly through building, demolition or rezoning. A house valued off the 2020 schedules may sit far from what a buyer would pay today. For each year from 2012 through 2025, the tax department posts a locational sales report. Read the report for your area and request your property record card before you argue about a value.

The lien runs from the January 1 listing date, so an inflated number costs money on every bill until 2028 arrives.

sections.h2: Tax rate, due date and late charges
sections.html:
Bertie's rate on the state's 2024-25 schedule is $.9300 per $100 of value. Each year the county board picks the rate, and towns levy a rate of their own on top. Use the current bill for the live rate.

Bertie County billing calendar
WhenResult
September 1Bill comes due
From September 1 to January 5No interest
January 62% interest attaches
After February 1Three-fourths of a percent added for each month or fraction of a month

A check sent by mail counts as paid on the postmark date, so keep the envelope or a receipt.

sections.h2: What happens when a bill stays open
sections.html:
If a bill sits unpaid, the county can sue in an action patterned on mortgage foreclosure. It ends with a public auction, and the winning bidder may need a deposit of up to 20%. You can still redeem until the court confirms the sale by paying the whole tax along with penalties, interest and costs. Selling the house during that stretch clears all of it at closing.

The county sells its own parcels through upset bids under G.S. 160A-269. A buyer's offer carries a 5% deposit and the newspaper runs a notice. For the next 10 days anyone may outbid it, raising the price by 10% of the first $1,000 plus 5% of whatever is above that. The board is free to reject any offer.

A primary home can get help from three state programs. One application covers all three, but you may claim just one. The tax page also hosts a physician certificate form for disability claims, a motor vehicle exemption form and a general exemption application.

With so many residents 65 or older, the elderly exclusion and the circuit breaker reach a large share of owners, and each owner must pass the application's income test.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: subtracts either $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger, if the owner is 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled. Income has to be under $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: subtracts the first $45,000 of value regardless of age or income. The disability must be permanent, total and tied to service, and a surviving spouse who has not remarried may claim it as well.
  • Circuit breaker: holds each year's tax to 4% of income, or 5% once income runs between the cap and 1.5 times the cap. Anything above that is deferred and stays on the property as a lien.

File with the county assessor. January is the normal window, and late filings are still accepted through June 1.

Plan around the board of equalization and review, which meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. You must file before it adjourns. If the notice reached you with fewer than 15 days left, you have 15 days from the mailing date instead. Rulings are mailed within a month, and anyone still unhappy has 30 days from that mailing to go to the Property Tax Commission. Take your property record card and the sales report for your area to the hearing.

sections.h2: Steps before you list a Bertie County house
sections.html: Begin with the tax record, which is the cheapest thing to fix early. Call (252) 794-5310 for the payoff on this year's bill and any older ones. Call (252) 794-5311 to check the parcel number, acreage and owner of record. Compare the square footage and condition on your property record card with what you know to be true. Find out what a sale does to any tax relief you receive. Finally, have the closing attorney order the payoff letter near the closing date so the number is still current on the day the deed is filed.

sections.h2: What a seller owes on the tax side at closing
sections.html:
The seller's proceeds pay off back and current bills. A payoff letter from the tax office gives the closing attorney a firm number.

Circuit breaker participants face one more charge: selling ends eligibility, and the last three years of deferred tax become due with interest.

Sellers also carry the state deed tax of $1.00 for every $500 of value or part of $500. It goes to the register before filing. A local recording resolution wants a return name and address, plus the buyer's permanent mailing address, printed on page one of every instrument.

An inherited title, tenants or deferred repairs change none of this. A lien payoff is identical whether the buyer finances or pays cash, and an as-is sale does not lift a lien before closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Bertie County tax office?
faqs.a: It works out of the county office building at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor. Phone (252) 794-5310 for bills and (252) 794-5311 for maps and parcel lookups.

faqs.q: What county tax rate does Bertie charge?
faqs.a: The state's 2024-25 schedule lists .9300 per $100. The rate for the current year is on your bill, and a town levy is added inside town limits.

faqs.q: When does Bertie County revalue next?
faqs.a: 2028 on the state's schedule, which is eight years after the January 1, 2020 reappraisal. A county can reappraise sooner but never later.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to challenge a Bertie County value?
faqs.a: You must file before the county board of equalization and review adjourns, or within 15 days of a late-mailed notice. Appeals to the Property Tax Commission follow within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

faqs.q: Can I buy a county-owned parcel in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Yes, by upset bid. Deliver a written offer and a 5% deposit to the county manager's office at 106 Dundee Street. A newspaper notice then starts a 10-day window for higher bids, and the board may turn down any offer.
